charity begins at home phrase

also near is my shirt, but nearer is my skin, look after number one

classical

Plaut. Trin. 1154: tunica propior palliōst

Tunica propior palliō est.

my tunic is nearer than my cloak: my own interest comes first

(vōx cōmica: Plaut.)

Lewis & Short s.v. tunica, comparing the English “near is my shirt, but nearer is my skin”.

Other words

  • Prīma cāritās incipit ā sē ipsō.

    also used · modern · Traupman 254

    We have found no ancient source for it in Lewis & Short or the loci collections.

Examples

  • hunc priōrem aequomst mē habēre: tunica propior palliōst

    it’s only right that I should put him first: my shirt is nearer than my coatPlaut. Trin. 1154

  • Meīs prius cōnsulam; tunica propior palliō est.

    I’ll see to my own first; charity begins at home.composed

SourcesLewis & Short: tunica

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency.

Plautus, Trinummus 1154.
